entities.summary:
The Battle of Voronezh was a pivotal Soviet victory against the German Wehrmacht during World War II, fought from June 28 to July 24, 1942. This battle took place on the Eastern Front in Voronezh, Russia, and was a crucial turning point in the war, as the Soviet Red Army successfully repelled the German advance and prevented the capture of the city.

The Battle of Voronezh was a testament to the bravery and resilience of the Soviet people, who suffered heavy losses but ultimately emerged victorious. The battle marked a significant shift in momentum on the Eastern Front, as the Soviet Union began to push the Germans back and eventually turn the tide of the war. The battle also showcased the effective use of Soviet tactics, such as the 'deep battle' strategy, which involved attacking the German rear and flanks.

The legacy of the Battle of Voronezh can be seen in the Soviet Union's continued push against the Germans, ultimately leading to the recapture of Stalingrad and the eventual defeat of Nazi Germany. The battle also marked a significant turning point in the war, as it prevented the Germans from capturing the city of Voronezh and thereby denied them a strategic victory. The battle remains an important chapter in the history of World War II and a testament to the bravery and sacrifice of the Soviet people.

The Battle of Voronezh will be remembered as a symbol of Soviet resistance against Nazi aggression and a testament to the power of human determination and perseverance.

The battle resulted in over 100,000 casualties and marked a turning point in the war on the Eastern Front.
